RELOCATION ASSISTANCE AGREEMENT -- SUMMARY

This Relocation Assistance Agreement ("Agreement") is between Meridian Analytics Inc. ("Company") and the employee accepting a position requiring relocation ("Employee"). It summarizes the terms of the relocation package offered as part of the Employee's offer letter.

1. Purpose. The Company recognizes that relocating for this role involves significant cost and disruption, and offers this package to offset reasonable, documented expenses associated with the move to the Company's primary office location.

2. Covered Expenses. The package covers: (a) professional moving company costs for household goods, up to $5,000; (b) temporary housing for up to 30 days while the Employee secures permanent housing; and (c) one round-trip house-hunting visit for the Employee and one accompanying family member prior to the move. The package does not cover pet transport costs or home staging costs for the Employee's previous residence; these remain the Employee's sole responsibility if incurred.

3. Payment Method. Covered expenses are either paid directly to vendors by the Company or reimbursed to the Employee within 15 business days of submitting itemized receipts. The Company may, at its discretion, issue up to half of the estimated package as an advance prior to the move, to be reconciled against actual receipts afterward.

4. Repayment Obligation. If the Employee voluntarily resigns, or is terminated for cause, within eighteen (18) months of their start date, the Employee must repay the Company a prorated portion of the total relocation package received, calculated as the number of months remaining in the 18-month period divided by 18, multiplied by the total package amount. If the Company terminates the Employee without cause at any point during the 18-month period, no repayment is owed by the Employee, regardless of how many months remain. Repayment, when owed, is due within 30 days of the Employee's separation date and may be deducted from final pay to the extent permitted by applicable law.

5. Tax Matters. Relocation reimbursements under this Agreement may be treated as taxable income to the Employee under current law. The Company will report such amounts as required and does not guarantee any particular tax treatment. Employees are encouraged to consult a tax advisor regarding their individual situation.

6. General Provisions. This Agreement does not alter the at-will nature of employment, where applicable, and does not guarantee employment for any specific duration. Any disputes arising under this Agreement will first be addressed through the Company's internal HR escalation process before any other remedy is pursued. This Agreement may be updated by the Company for employees hired after the effective date of any such update, but changes will not apply retroactively to packages already disbursed. The Company will provide the Employee with a copy of the then-current policy at the time of the offer letter, and any subsequent amendments will be communicated in writing at least 30 days before taking effect for that Employee. Nothing in this Agreement limits either party's other rights or obligations under the Employee's separate offer letter or any applicable collective bargaining agreement, to the extent one exists.

7. Definitions. For purposes of this Agreement, "start date" means the first day the Employee reports to work in the new location in an active-employee capacity, not the date of hire or the date of the offer letter. "Separation date" means the last day the Employee is on the Company's active payroll, regardless of the reason for separation. These definitions govern the calculations in Section 4 above.

Case Note (Personnel File, Sept 20): Employee received a total relocation package of $9,000, disbursed in full at the time of the move. Employee voluntarily resigned 6 months after their start date to accept a position at another firm. No termination for cause or involuntary termination is on record.
